People's Majlis Committee Minutes

8th meeting of the Environment and Climate Change Committee

3 August 2026

Venue of the meeting: People's Majlis building (Committee Room 6)

Start time: 11:00

{Presiding: Chair of the Committee; Member for South Maafannu constituency Abdulla Rifau}

The Chair:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. I welcome all members to the 8th meeting of the People's Majlis Environment and Climate Change Committee. The meeting is being held in Committee Room 6. The date is 3 August 2026, Monday. The time is 11:10. On today's agenda is the review of the Bill to amend Law No. 24/2022 (Waste Management Act). This Bill has come to this committee because the Committee of the Whole House assigned this work to the Environment Committee as a sub-committee. So, we have now set 10 October as the deadline for completing this work. So, present at this committee at this time are myself (Member for South Maafannu constituency Abdulla Rifau), Member for Central Hulhumale' constituency Abdulla Shazeem, Member for Hithaadhoo constituency Mohamed Siruhaan, Member for Gemanafushi constituency Asadhulla Shihab, Member for South Thinadhoo constituency Mohamed Alsan Ahmed, and Member for North Hithadhoo constituency Abdulla Sodig. So, we will proceed with this Bill by going through each article of the Bill. So, I ask the secretariat to put the Bill up on the screen. The Member for Mulaku constituency Ibrahim Naufal has joined the committee. As decided at the previous committee meeting, we have now opened it for comments from the relevant institutions. We should receive these comments by today. It has also been opened for public opinion. So, once the comments are received, if a comment comes in on any article we are reviewing, we will proceed in a way that lets us go back to that article later. The proposal submitted to amend this law is now visible on the screen. Making the following amendments to Law No. 24/2022 (Waste Management Act). First, 1- Amending article 8(h) of the said law as follows. 8(h)- Setting a waste management policy suited to each island or area in islands and areas allocated for economic and/or industrial activities. 2- Of the said law; while this is being read, if there is any comment, just signal and I will give the floor for that comment. Amending article 8(p) of the said law as follows.

[stamp]

8(p)- Designing and establishing waste management systems and setting the standards to be maintained in managing waste through those systems. 3- Amending article 8(q) of the said law as follows. Article 8(q). Setting the standards for establishing waste management centres and the standards for establishing centres that carry out the safe disposal of waste. 4- Amending article 8(r) of the said law as follows. 8(r)- Formulating the principles for determining the areas in which waste management centres and centres that carry out the safe disposal of waste are to be established. 5- Amending article 8(s) of the said law as follows. Article 8(s). Setting the standards that equipment used to establish a waste management system must meet and the standards for testing and certifying that equipment. The Member for West Maafannu constituency Mohamed Musthafa has joined the committee. 6- Adding a clause after article 8(s) of the said law as follows. Article 8(t). Making all the regulations that need to be made to implement this law and setting the standards that need to be set. 7- Adding two clauses after article 9(c) of the said law as follows. 9(d)- Planning and carrying out everything that needs to be done to implement the regulations made and standards set by the Ministry under this law in relation to waste management. (e)- In cases where waste management contrary to the standards set by the Ministry under this law causes an undesirable impact on the environment and/or public health, fining the parties acting in that way in accordance with the regulation made by the Environmental Regulatory Authority under this law. 8- Amending article 10(c) of the said law as follows. 10(c)- Setting, in the regulation made under this law, the standards and principles to be followed in providing waste management services in accordance with the policies formulated and the standards and principles set by the Ministry under this law, enforcing those principles and standards, and taking the necessary action against parties that breach them. 9- Removing article 10(d) of the said law. 10- Amending article 10(i) of the said law as follows. 10(i)- Notwithstanding anything stated otherwise in this law or in any other law, in islands and areas allocated for carrying out economic and/or industrial activities

[stamp]

ensuring that a waste management system suited to that island or area is being operated sustainably. And 11- Amending the heading of article 12 of the said law and article 12(a) as follows. Management of waste generated in islands and areas allocated for economic or industrial activities. 12(a)- Waste management in islands and areas allocated for carrying out economic and/or industrial activities is the responsibility of the owner of that island or area or the party managing it. 12- Amending article 24 of the said law as follows. Plan for managing waste generated by economic activities. 24(a)- An operational plan setting out how waste management will be carried out for waste generated at places engaged in tourism, agriculture, fisheries and other such economic activities must be formulated by the owner of that place or the party managing that place, in accordance with the regulation made under this law. (b)- Implementing the operational plan described in (a) of this article is the responsibility of the owner of that place or the party managing that place. (c)- The operational plan for managing waste generated by economic activities prepared under (a) of this article must be a plan formulated in accordance with the National Waste Management Master Plan and the island and city level or regional level waste management operational plan. 13- Adding an article after article 24 of the said law as follows. Industrial waste management plan. 24-1 (a) An operational plan setting out how waste management will be carried out for waste generated at places engaged in an industrial activity must be formulated by the owner of that place or a party managing that place, in accordance with the regulation made under this law. (b)- Implementing the operational plan described in (a) of this article is the responsibility of the owner of that place, the management of that place and that party. (b)- In (a) of this article; Member for Gemanafushi constituency Asadhulla.

Member for Gemanafushi constituency Asadhulla Shihab:

[stamp]

Thank you, honourable Chair. Now, this operational plan for managing waste generated at places engaged in industrial activities, you know, that is something that already exists. Something that already exists. But what happens is that even in the earlier article the operational plan is there, isn't it, stating that it must fit the national waste disposal policy. In reality, the way things happen in the Maldives now is that even at the resorts being built now and on islands engaged in industrial activities, waste is disposed of, well, this is not about everyone. The way it is done in many of these places is simply by digging a conventional pit and burning the waste. Burning it, and then, to make it fit that standard, some amount of waste is sent out to Thilafushi. So, I do not yet see the articles written in the law there as something that looks at the real problem here and brings a solution to the real problem. That is, it is done the way I described. Pits are simply dug, all kinds of waste are dumped into the same pit, and whether at night or in the daytime they are simply burned, and to fit the standard some amount of waste is sent out to Thilafushi. But in reality the waste is disposed of in the most haphazard way, contrary to laws and regulations. So, what I think in this law is that what needs strengthening here is perhaps a monitoring plan for this. As it is written here now, I am not yet clear about the part that follows. Now, waste management, and implementing that law, is set out here as the responsibility of the owner of that place or else the responsibility of the party managing it. If so, the question is whether there is a monitoring plan for this.

The Chair:

As this law has been designed, it will be this authority, the Environmental Regulatory Authority, that oversees its enforcement and imposes whatever fines need to be imposed. They will carry out the monitoring work. Then, as far as the follow-up goes, the regulation made along with this, the regulations made under this law, detail these parts extensively. Member for North Hithadhoo constituency Abdulla Sodig.

[stamp]

Member for North Hithadhoo constituency Abdulla Sodig:

The monitoring by this authority is made obligatory on the authority in this law, and it is also in an article being amended. But how far it can be monitored is something that has to be determined, even if through the regulation that is made. For example, many things like this could be considered, such as whether there should be someone to monitor large projects in a manner determined by the authority. But this law does include fines and those matters. So, what needs to be strengthened is the way it is monitored, that process.

The Chair:

So, I will proceed. 13(c)- (a) of this article, the 13th amendment, adding an article after article 24 of the said law as follows. Its 24(1)(c). The industrial waste management plan prepared under (a) of this article, the operational plan, must be a plan formulated in accordance with the National Waste Management Master Plan and the island and city level or regional level waste management operational plan. 14- Adding a clause after article 25(b) of the said law as follows. 25(c)- The regulation made under (b) of this article must determine licence categories having regard to the types of waste set out under this law, and must set out the principles and procedures for issuing a licence of each category and the principles for setting additional conditions in licences so issued. 15- Adding a number after number 3 of article 32(b) of the said law as follows. 32(b)(4)- A pack of plastic bags containing more than 50 bags, this comes under the exemption article. The article on exemption from tax collection. Yes! Member for North Hithadhoo constituency Abdulla Sodig.

Member for North Hithadhoo constituency Abdulla Sodig:

At what point is the 50-bag exemption? At wholesale level or at retail level? If a retail shop sells 50 bags at a time, then, not required even at a retail shop.

[stamp]

So then everyone should buy the 50-bag packs. But retail now... from the wholesaler. Now, the purpose of this is that this point is being raised because it would be double taxed. So, actually from the wholesaler...

The Chair:

As it is time for voting on the floor, we will adjourn the committee at this point, so that the committee continues again after the vote. Thank you. (After a short break) Yes! Thank you. We will end this committee at this point, so that we continue with the remaining part, together with the comments, at the next meeting to be held. Thank you very much.
